source.title: Large scale distributed neural network training through online distillation
source.authors: Rohan Anil; Gabriel Pereyra; A. Passos; Róbert Ormándi; G. Dahl; Geoffrey E. Hinton

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares validation accuracy across batch sizes on ImageNet, a related test of the large-batch claim, but does not report the fixed-epoch comparison the version specifies.
record.gate_note: The paper reports many codistillation and prediction-churn results, but these do not measure the training–test generalization gap named in the versions. Figure 3 includes a 32k-batch synchronous SGD curve alongside a 16k-batch baseline; the text does not describe that curve's outcome.
record.test_reason: The study varies batch size and measures held-out performance on ImageNet and Common Crawl, bearing on V5. However, the supplied text does not establish the outcome at matched epoch budgets, so it cannot support a directional verdict.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly correct: the authors conclude that codistillation improves training speed and model quality using additional parallelism and reduces prediction churn. They also explicitly report diminishing returns from increasing batch size, but do not establish a fixed-epoch large-batch generalization penalty.
record.recipe_differences: The ImageNet experiment plots validation accuracy by training step for synchronous SGD at 16k and 32k batch sizes; the version concerns held-out performance under a fixed epoch budget and the train–test gap.
record.method_sensitivity: ImageNet batch size (16k versus 32k) is varied in Figure 3; the text does not describe the comparative result.

fits_no_version.finding: On Common Crawl, increasing synchronous workers beyond 128 provides no additional step-count improvement and worsens wall-clock progress.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing batch size eventually stops improving optimization efficiency, with infrastructure overhead further limiting distributed training.

fits_no_version.finding: ImageNet codistillation reaches 75% accuracy at 5250 steps versus 7250 for the baseline, and reaches 75.6% at 7250 steps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Online distillation can improve held-out accuracy and reduce training steps using additional parallel resources.

fits_no_version.finding: Codistillation reduces prediction churn by approximately 35% on Criteo.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Online distillation improves prediction reproducibility across retraining runs.

record.problems: The relevant batch-size comparison is presented only as a figure, without textual interpretation, numerical values, uncertainty, or a stated fixed epoch budget. The paper does not report training error for this comparison.
record.rows_left_out: No other reported results directly measure the claim versions' behaviors. Codistillation accuracy and prediction-churn experiments concern different outcomes.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under comparable tuning.
The held-out performance penalty at a matched epoch budget is not established in the supplied text. Longer training and recipe changes are not isolated as remedies for that penalty.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Removing highly memorized examples versus removing random examples.

missing.what: The Common Crawl batch-size sweep is omitted: effective batches range from 4096 to 32768, with learning rates tuned separately. The authors identify 128 workers, batch 16384, as their strongest configuration for training time and final accuracy. Record the held-out cross-entropy comparisons, distinguishing step-count and wall-clock outcomes from any matched-example comparison; the supplied figure text does not provide readable curve values.

record.verdict_notes: V5 concerns held-out performance and does not require reporting a training–test gap. Missing training error is therefore not the decisive limitation here; the unreadable curve comparison and unmatched training budgets are.

versions.untested_parts: Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD on held-out performance.
The paper plots validation accuracy for 16k- and 32k-batch synchronous SGD on ImageNet, but does not state the comparative outcome in text or specify a fixed epoch budget.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the generalization gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test accuracy.

rows.subject: Sync 32k batch size
rows.operation_detail: Synchronous SGD trained with a 32k batch size; validation accuracy is plotted against training step.
rows.note: The figure legend identifies the 32k and 16k synchronous batch-size curves, but the accompanying text does not state their relative outcomes or an epoch-budget comparison.
rows.check: The supplied figure text identifies the 16k and 32k curves but does not reveal their relative accuracy. Equal training steps also imply different numbers of examples processed across batch sizes; a fixed-epoch comparison is not established.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
